title_en: Chinese Humor (15/20): Outwitting a Smart Speaker
note_en: To say that something was heard or recorded wrongly, Chinese uses 把A + verb + 成B: 自己的音箱有一次把「关灯」听成了「关天」 "his speaker once heard 'turn off the light' as 'turn off the sky.'" The verb says how the mistake happened (听 hear, 记 record, 当 regard), and 成 marks what A turned into. English needs "mishear... as" or "mistake... for"; Chinese can attach 成 to almost any verb, as in 系统居然把他说的话记成了完全不同的东西.

sentences.en: Smart speakers mishearing commands are so maddening and funny largely because Chinese has a huge number of homophones: with even a slight accent, yinyue ("music") can be recognized as some other similar-sounding word. Netizens like to joke that smart speakers aren't artificial intelligence but "artificial stupidity."
